subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific URL/domain/path denylist or warnlist, or fold this into a broader cross-tool egress policy?
rationale: The requested behavior would create operator-facing security/config surface, and the related open issues show competing browser-only, private-network, and generic egress scopes that automation should not choose on its own.

options.title: Design Browser Policy First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn semantics for domains, paths, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, docs, and tests.

options.title: Fold Into Generic Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-policy work the canonical direction if maintainers want one policy for browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP access.

options.title: Reject Browser Denylist Surface
options.body: Close this after documenting that bot-blocked public domains remain an operator workflow concern outside OpenClaw config.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn semantics for domains, paths, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal across browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard behavior, proxy-routing hardening, and shared SSRF policy design.
